entry.title: On paper, a bitcoin key now takes 20,000 to 30,000 qubits, not 500,000; IBM's best chip has 120
entry.summary: Google said under 500,000 in March. IonQ's blueprint in September gives 19,397 trapped-ion qubits and 26 days a try; Alice & Bob's in October at most 30,000 cat qubits and about an hour. The Bank of Thailand is taking stock of its locks.
entry.content:
The quantum computer that works out a bitcoin private key from its public key keeps shrinking on paper. Google Quantum AI said on 31 March 2026 that the job takes fewer than 1,200 to 1,450 logical qubits, or fewer than 500,000 physical superconducting qubits running for a few minutes, about 20 times fewer than earlier estimates. A logical qubit is one error-free unit of the calculation; a physical qubit is one piece of hardware, and it takes many of them, checking one another, to make one logical qubit. On 8 September IonQ published a blueprint for a trapped-ion machine: 1,457 logical qubits on 19,397 physical qubits, 39 million Toffoli gates, 25.7 days per attempt, a size IonQ places on its own roadmap around 2028. On 28 October Alice & Bob posted a compilation for cat qubits, a superconducting design that suppresses one of the two kinds of qubit error: RSA-2048, the lock on much of the web, in about 23,000 cat qubits and 3.14 days, and a secp256k1 key, bitcoin's curve, in at most about 30,000 cat qubits and about an hour, assuming a phase-flip error rate of 5 in 10,000 and no bit-flips at all. A paper by Luo and colleagues, posted in July and revised in September, cut the logical count itself to 835, from 1,098 and 1,175 in the two best earlier designs.

The three physical counts are three different machines, so 500,000, 19,397 and 30,000 are not one series. No built machine is near any of them in error-corrected qubits. IBM's Nighthawk, named on 5 November as its most powerful processor, has 120 qubits; Google's Willow has 105. IBM says it has run experiments with up to 70 logical qubits and 438 hard operations, against a US Department of Energy target of 100 logical qubits running 100,000 hard operations by late 2028, a gap of about 230 times. On 19 October Quantinuum reported a logical fidelity of 99.9995% on its Helios machine, five errors per million operations, ten times better than its September record, with each step up in code distance cutting the remaining errors by a factor of 12, at up to 37 physical qubits per logical qubit; it dates Apollo, its fault-tolerant machine, to 2029. IonQ says a fault-tolerant 10,000-qubit system is due in 2027.

On timing, a June 2026 paper by Gershteyn and Alber, Quantum Horizon, ran a Monte Carlo forecast over hardware scaling, falling resource estimates and expert surveys and got a two-peaked spread: about a one-in-six chance of a key-breaking machine by 2035, about 30% by 2040, about 60% by 2050. It counts about 6 million BTC in quantum-exposed addresses, of which about 2.3 million no migration can protect; Google's whitepaper counted about 6.9 million exposed. NIST's final transition report of 27 October 2026 deprecates ECDSA, EdDSA and RSA after 2030 and disallows them after 2035.

In Thailand the same locks sit under PromptPay, mobile banking and the exchanges. The Bank of Thailand's page on emerging payment technologies says it is taking an inventory of its own cryptography, planning swaps to NIST's post-quantum standards FIPS 203, 204 and 205 through one central layer so an algorithm changes once, and ran a Quantum Board Awareness Seminar for bank boards on 18 March 2026; its migration report is marked "soon". A coin on Bitkub or Binance TH sits under the exchange's keys; a coin in a wallet of one's own sits under the key of its address, and bitcoin shows that key on the chain once the address has spent, or from the start for a Taproot address.

entry.title: Dollar stablecoins fell $8.4 billion in eleven days, the steepest week of 2026
entry.summary: Ten straight days down from 29 October, the day of the Binance theft, to the lowest total since September 2025. Tether froze over $1.5 billion of the stolen USDT; the Bank of Thailand counts USDT flows in hundreds of billions of baht.
entry.content:
On DefiLlama's count, dollar stablecoins in circulation stood at $301.6 billion on 28 October 2026 and $293.2 billion on 7 November, down $8.4 billion in eleven days, falling on every one of the ten days from 29 October, the day thieves took $6.3 billion from Binance. 8 November added $0.07 billion back. The seven days to 4 November lost $5.8 billion, the steepest week of 2026 on DefiLlama's chart; the week Terra's UST collapsed in May 2022 lost $27.4 billion. The total is the lowest since 26 September 2025. The peak was $315.5 billion on 17 May; a year ago, on 8 November 2025, the figure was $302.5 billion. On 30 October Offrampt read the same series as flat for a year. It is not flat now.

USDT, the largest, went from $184.3 billion on 9 October to $179.6 billion on 2 November and $176.8 billion on 9 November, on DefiLlama's figures; USDC from $73.3 billion to $71.9 billion and $70.6 billion. Both still trade at about one dollar, USDT at $0.9989 and USDC at $0.9998 on 9 November. Tether's attestation for the third quarter, prepared by the accounting firm BDO and published on 30 October, gave $184 billion of USDT issued on 30 September, $191.5 billion of reserve assets, and a buffer of $7.95 billion above what it owes holders; its net operating profit for the quarter was $1.5 billion. A theft on its own does not shrink the supply: it shrinks when a holder hands coins back to the issuer for dollars and the issuer destroys them. GN Crypto reports that neither Tether nor Circle, which issues USDC, has linked the fall to the Binance theft.

On 2 November Tether said it had frozen more than $1.5 billion of USDT within 30 minutes of the Binance attack, which the FBI attributes to North Korea. By 31 October, Tether says, it had frozen about 1.6 billion USDT across more than 3,590 wallets for the US Department of Justice, Secret Service and FBI, and over its history more than 7 billion USDT on addresses on the open market, of which about 1.2 billion has gone back to its owners or to law enforcement through reissue. Frozen USDT stays on the chain and cannot move; it is still counted in the supply until Tether destroys and reissues it.

In Thailand USDT is the coin the central bank is counting. On 28 January 2026 Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said USDT was 52% of crypto trading volume in Thailand and about 40% of the people trading it on Thai exchanges were foreigners, and asked the SEC for the trading data. On 2 October he put abnormal conversion through foreign exchange and stablecoins such as USDT at several hundred billion baht over the previous four to five months, with cases of money withdrawn to buy USDT and sent abroad under other people's names. On Bitkub's own order book USDT was 50.7% of baht trading on 6 November. The SEC's September proposal, a 5 million baht daily cap per operator and transfers only to a customer's own verified wallet, is on the rules page. The Bank of Thailand plans rules for a baht stablecoin in March 2027; the hearing on its principles runs to 17 November. In the plan, a foreigner holds the coin only in a verified Thai wallet, and an issuer must be able to freeze or destroy coins used illegally.

entry.title: The SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget; Thailand blocks it from 5 December
entry.summary: Sixteen days earlier Bitget said it would buy a licensed Thai exchange; that deal needs the SEC's approval. Block dates set by the SEC: one in 2025, five in 2026, the last three inside ten weeks.
entry.content:
On 5 November 2026 the Thai Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed a criminal complaint with the Economic Crime Suppression Division against BG Limited, the company behind bitget.com, for running a digital asset exchange without a Thai licence. The same day it sent Bitget's website, its other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, to block access from Thailand from 5 December. The SEC's notice asks Bitget users to act on the assets they have on the platform before that date. A complaint opens a police inquiry; a prosecutor and then a court decide the case.

The SEC says that from 2022 to 2025 Bitget ran a trading system and charged fees, with a Thai-language website showing values in baht, and promoted itself in Thai through accounts named "Bitget Thailand" on X, "BGB Thai Holder" on Telegram and "bitgetthailand" on TikTok. The complaint also names one person as a supporter, for promoting Bitget on a Facebook page and a YouTube channel; Cointelegraph reports the SEC named the same person in March 2025 over promoting OKX. Bitget has been on the SEC's Investor Alert list of unlicensed operators since 8 May 2023. Bitget had not answered Cointelegraph's request for comment on 5 November.

Sixteen days before the complaint, on 20 October, Bitget announced a plan to buy GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok exchange and broker licensed since July 2020. The buyer is BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd., set up on 22 September 2026 with share capital of 2 million baht, according to the seller, Japan's GMO Internet. GMO's filing gave 31 October as the expected date of transfer and says BTGT's major shareholders will follow the Thai SEC's rule on approving major shareholders. Bitget's release says it brings its platform to Thai users only after the deal closes and the change of control is approved. The exchange lost 87.6 million baht in 2025 on sales of 11.0 million. On 24 September, the day GMO's board approved the sale, thieves took about $388 million from Bitget's hot and warm wallets (the wallets an exchange pays daily withdrawals from) without needing its private keys, Unchained reports; withdrawals reopened in phases from 28 September.

Bitget is the sixth block date on Offrampt's list since the law changed. The Royal Decree on technology crime (No. 2), in force since 13 April 2025, lets the ministry block unlicensed digital asset trading platforms; the SEC sends it the names. The dates: 28 June 2025 for Bybit, OKX, CoinEx, XT.COM and 1000X; 22 March 2026 for Bitazza Global; 2 May for Exmix; 1 October for the Holdstation and UNO apps; 7 November for Vcex.io, whose owner As Sure Technology and four people the SEC filed against on 7 October; and 5 December for Bitget. Each block date sits 30 or 31 days after the SEC's complaint or referral. Binance.com, Pionex and MEXC are on the Investor Alert list without a block date; in its 30 October statement on the Binance theft the SEC called binance.com the overseas Binance platform, not under its supervision.

entry.title: Myanmar's CI card now needs three months of bank remittances; applications fell within days
entry.summary: Five CI centres opened in Thailand on 14 October. A worker shows 25% of pay sent home through official channels and a year of income tax. Official channels pay 125 kyat a baht; the informal market pays over 130.
entry.content:
A Certificate of Identity (CI) is the Myanmar travel paper a worker in Thailand uses in place of a passport to hold a work permit. Myanmar's government opened five CI centres in Thailand on 14 October 2026, running to 14 January 2027: Samut Sakhon, Samut Prakan, Surat Thani and Chiang Mai, with a mobile unit in Chonburi. An applicant now shows proof of one year of Myanmar income tax (the 2% levy on earnings abroad) and three months of remittances through official channels, the Labour Ministry's rule that 25% of pay goes home through licensed banks and transfer firms. Burma News International puts the remittance at 2,000 baht a month, 6,000 over three months, the tax at about 1,800 baht a year, and the CI fee at 2,660 baht, paid at 7-Eleven.

On 18 October workers started an online campaign asking Thailand for permits without the CI. The Irrawaddy reported on 27 October that the Samut Sakhon centre, which took over 1,000 applications a day, had gone quiet; the Aid Alliance Committee counts at least 500,000 workers due to apply. Labour Minister Maung Myint said on 20 October that about 1,500 workers had used the centres in the first days. Agents and activists told the paper a CI without remittance evidence costs 1,500 baht in bribes. On the rate: official channels pay 125 kyat per baht, the informal market over 130, so a worker gives up at least 5,000 kyat on every 100 baht sent the official way.

Naypyitaw is pressing from its side. At an inter-ministerial meeting on 30 October the minister put routing overseas earnings through the Central Bank of Myanmar and licensed firms first, and the central bank is reading the records of True Money, 2C2P, K-Bank and Dee Money (Eleven Media, 1 November). From 1 November a worker going back abroad applies in Yangon with proof of the 2% tax and remittance records for the three months before the return, through central-bank authorised banks or holders of a Remittance Business License. Remittances were US$5.6 billion in 2025, and the ministry's goal is the same figure for 2026.

Bangkok is hearing the other side. On 2 November the White Employers group told a parliamentary security committee that the levy comes to about 6,000 baht a worker, paid through TrueMoney and again at 7-Eleven, that passport-related fees rose from 310 baht to 710 and then 2,670, and that brokers ask 1,350 to 1,500 baht for a queue place already booked; employers advance the money for workers who cannot. Nation Thailand gives about 700,000 workers needing a CI and over a million passports near expiry. The People's Party called the 2% tax inconsistent with the 2002 Thailand–Myanmar double taxation agreement and asked for CI centres under Thai supervision.

The Financial Action Task Force, the body that sets anti-money-laundering standards, kept Myanmar on its call-for-action list on 30 October and will consider countermeasures if there is no progress by February 2027; Myanmar's delegation says 13 of the 15 items on its action plan are done. The statement asks countries to keep remittances "neither disrupted nor discouraged" and says it will watch whether Myanmar's own checks "apply undue scrutiny to legitimate financial flows".

entry.title: Binance reopened withdrawals three days after the $6.3 billion theft
entry.summary: Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen coins with its own money. Mt. Gox took ten years to start paying back; FTX took over two.
entry.content:
Binance lost about US$6.3 billion from its hot wallets (wallets kept online so withdrawals can go out fast) on 29 and 30 October 2026. On 31 October it said it had covered up to 90% of the stolen assets; on 1 November, about 95%. The money came from its SAFU reserve fund, part of its futures insurance fund and its company treasury. Co-CEO Yi He said Binance would use half of the $1 billion SAFU fund and fill it back up.

Withdrawals reopened on Sunday 1 November, bitcoin first, at about 13:00 Thai time. The first phase covers 15 coins, among them BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC and XRP. The last 5% is coins outside the top ten, which Binance says are harder to buy in size. Since the reopening, users have taken out about $3.6 billion, Siam Blockchain reported, citing Cointelegraph. Binance's 2025 annual report gives $162.8 billion in customer assets.

About $3 billion of the stolen coins stay frozen, mostly USDT and USDC; bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen this way. On 31 October the FBI named North Korea's TraderTraitor unit and said the thieves had turned the coins into ether. Co-CEO Richard Teng called it a complex attack, with hacked laptops and malware built to erase its traces.

Binance TH is a separate company, Gulf Binance, licensed by the Thai SEC. It paused crypto withdrawals on 30 October while baht kept moving. The reports read for this note, up to 2 November, cover Binance.com's reopening and give no date for Binance TH.

entry.title: Binance paused withdrawals after a $6.3 billion theft
entry.summary: The largest crypto theft on record began, Binance says, with one engineer's laptop. Binance TH paused crypto withdrawals; baht kept moving.
entry.content:
Binance says it lost about US$6.3 billion on 29 and 30 October 2026, and paused deposits and withdrawals. Its first check points to one DevOps engineer's laptop as the way in. TRM Labs names North Korea's TraderTraitor group, the group the FBI named for Bybit's $1.5 billion loss in February 2025.

About $3 billion of the stolen coins were frozen on-chain: Tether froze over $1.5 billion of USDT, and Circle $800 million of USDC. Binance says it will cover all losses. Its SAFU reserve fund held about $1 billion at its 2024 disclosure.

In Thailand, Binance TH (Gulf Binance, licensed by the SEC) paused crypto withdrawals, while baht deposits, baht withdrawals and trading kept running, Thansettakij reported. The Thai SEC said it had found no significant impact on Thai customers' assets so far, and told licensed firms to check and report. Bitcoin traded under $77,000.

entry.title: The long view: crypto is not actually crypto
entry.summary: Keys leak through laptops and flawed code, and on paper the machine that breaks bitcoin's math keeps getting smaller.
entry.content:
Everything leaks. Chainalysis counted $3.7 billion stolen from crypto businesses in 2022, $1.7 billion in 2023, $2.2 billion in 2024 and over $3.4 billion in 2025. CertiK counts $2.68 billion from January to September 2026, before Binance's $6.3 billion in October. In August 2026, attackers drained over $130 million from Coldcard hardware wallets, offline ones among them, through a 2021 flaw that made seed phrases predictable.

On paper, the math gets cheaper to break. For RSA-2048, a common lock on the web, estimates of the quantum computer needed fell from 20 million noisy qubits (2019) to under 1 million (Google, May 2025) to under 100,000 (an Iceberg Quantum preprint, February 2026). For the 256-bit elliptic curve under bitcoin's keys, Google estimated in March 2026 under half a million physical qubits running for minutes, about a 20-fold cut from earlier estimates. Google's Willow chip, shown in December 2024, has 105 qubits.

Google's paper counts about 6.9 million BTC in addresses whose public keys are already exposed or reused. NIST's final guidance of 27 October 2026 deprecates RSA, ECDSA and EdDSA after 2030 and disallows them after 2035. Bitcoin's BIP-360, a draft that hides keys from long-exposure attacks, entered the proposals list in February 2026 and is not active.

Used as a tool, crypto moves value where a Thai bank account is out of reach, and the move takes minutes. Held for decades, it rests on locks with a date on them.

entry.title: A Thai bank account depends on your visa, and one flag stops them all
entry.summary: Kasikornbank's published list leaves out the DTV and short-stay visas. Since 2024, a fraud flag on a person stops every account that person holds.
entry.content:
No Bank of Thailand rule lists which visas a bank must accept; each bank sets its own. Kasikornbank opens savings accounts for any Non-Immigrant visa with documents for the purpose of stay, and not for the TR visa, short-stay visas or the DTV. SCB lists a passport and a work permit. Bangkok Bank opens accounts in person at a branch in Thailand, not from abroad. Since January 2025, Bangkok Bank has stopped opening accounts for short-stay visitors and counts DTV holders among them, The Phuket Express and The Thaiger reported in May 2025.

Since 1 August 2024, Thai banks share suspect data through the Central Fraud Registry: when a person is flagged, electronic channels stop on all of that person's accounts until verification. Since January 2025, banks can suspend outgoing transfers before any victim reports a loss. In September 2026, the Bank of Thailand and 11 industry bodies adopted a framework to tighten customer checks again.

Without a Thai account, crypto still reaches baht: on Offrampt's calculator on 30 October, the two crypto-card routes draw cash at a Thai ATM for 3% to 6% less than the mid-market rate.

entry.title: Dollar stablecoins stopped growing this year
entry.summary: $304.7 billion a year ago, a $315.5 billion peak in May, $299.6 billion now. Thailand is narrowing the doors for USDT at the same time.
entry.content:
On DefiLlama's count, dollar stablecoins in circulation stood at $304.7 billion on 30 October 2025, peaked at $315.5 billion on 17 May 2026, and stand at $299.6 billion on 30 October 2026. In July, Forbes reported the fall after the May peak as the first in four years. June 2026 still set a volume record of $1.79 trillion.

USDT is 37% of the baht trading on Bitkub's own order book on 30 October; on other days of the past month it has been near half.

In Thailand the Bank of Thailand has screened abnormally large USDT trades since July 2026. In September the SEC proposed a 5 million baht daily cap per operator and an own-wallet rule for stablecoin transfers. On 30 October Tether froze over $1.5 billion of USDT taken from Binance.

entry.title: Thai crypto rules: a new step about every four weeks
entry.summary: 13 changes in twelve months. Each narrows the road between a wallet and a Thai bank account to licensed firms and the customer's own verified wallets.
entry.content:
Offrampt's rules timeline holds 13 Thai changes from 31 October 2025 to 30 October 2026. The latest six: 2026-09-14: The OECD lists Thailand among jurisdictions starting crypto tax data exchanges (CARF) by 2028; 2026-09-11: The SEC proposes a 5 million baht daily cap per operator and an own-wallet rule for stablecoin transfers; comment closes 25 September; 2026-09-07: The SEC imposes civil sanctions on four people for manipulating trading volume of the SIX Network token; 2026-09-02: The SEC issues the crypto Travel Rule, effective 27 February 2027; 2026-09-01: The SEC names Tools for Humanity and its CEO as supporters of the unlicensed UNO app; Holdstation and UNO are to be blocked from 1 October; 2026-08-25: The Cabinet approves a draft Act amending the Digital Asset Decree, sending it to Parliament.

Two dates sit ahead: the Travel Rule takes effect on 27 February 2027, and Thailand starts sharing crypto tax data with other countries under the OECD's CARF by 2028.

entry.title: Scam losses in Thailand: from 117 million baht a day to about 50 million
entry.summary: Police figures for early 2024 against the Anti-Cyber Scam Centre's for the first half of 2026. The loss per case is above 52,000 baht.
entry.content:
Royal Thai Police data put reported online losses at an average of 117 million baht a day in early 2024, and 65 million in February 2025, after the border cut-offs that month.

For January to June 2026, nearly 9 billion baht was lost across more than 170,000 cases, about 50 million baht a day. The average loss was above 52,000 baht a case, and Facebook was linked to over 61% of cases (Thailand Consumers Council).

The two series count in different ways, police reports against scam complaints, so the fall is a direction, not an exact rate.

entry.title: Money home to Myanmar: 93% of senders use informal channels
entry.summary: Hundi costs about 2.5%, banks about 10%, and the kyat has lost about 80% against the dollar since 2021.
entry.content:
About 1.75 million Myanmar citizens worked in Thailand officially in October 2023 (AMRO). A study by the Institute for Strategic Policy, reported by Thai PBS World in September 2026, says 93% of Myanmar remitters in Thailand used informal channels (IOM's 2024 survey), 60% used hundi agents, and about 68% of Myanmar's informal remittances come from Thailand. Hundi costs about 2.5%, against about 10% at banks in the past. The kyat has lost about 80% against the dollar since 2021.

Myanmar's Labour Ministry ordered overseas workers in 2023 to send 25% of earnings home through approved banks at a fixed rate; one worker reported 2,940 kyat per dollar against a market rate of 3,500 (Radio Free Asia). In May 2024 the Central Bank of Myanmar warned against unregulated digital currencies and acted against hundi transfers made with USDT (Tilleke & Gibbins).

In Thailand, USDT trades on licensed exchanges from 16 March 2025, and the SEC's September 2026 proposal would limit stablecoin transfers to the customer's own verified wallets.
